AccessibilitySettings.description:
BL-065, 2.1.27. **POS and kiosk accessibility, which is a legal obligation in most jurisdictions and was unstated.**
**A kiosk is the hard case.** A guest with low vision using a website brings their own assistive technology; a guest at a kiosk gets whatever the kiosk offers, so the settings have to be on the device rather than in the browser.

reachableHeightModeAvailable.description: **Moves the interface to the lower half of the screen** for a guest using a wheelchair. A kiosk mounted at standing height is unusable otherwise, and no software setting fixes the mounting — this is the mitigation.

sessionTimeoutMultiplier.description: **Timeouts are an accessibility barrier nobody counts.** A guest who needs three times as long to read a screen should not lose their basket to a 90-second inactivity timer.

AppAvailability.description: **The sold-out or closed signal (decided 28 September, audit R073).** `open` is the normal state. `soldOut` shows WEB-029's sold-out state across the app while browsing still works; `closed` shows the closed state (a weather closure, a private event). Neither refuses a request on its own: it is what the guest is told, and a sale is still refused by availability where it applies. Set with `setMaintenanceMode`.

derived.description: Generated by `setAppIcons` from the source, one entry per platform and size — the iOS and Android store sets and the web favicons listed on `setAppIcons` (audit R163). Asked of Assets as renditions, an entry is pending, with no `assetRef`, until its rendition is ready (ADAM CR-106).

changeScope.description: Always `buildTime` — icons are baked into the binary.

liveVersion.description: Icon currently shipped. Differs from the draft until the next release. **Where it comes from** (ADAM CR-325, option A, 29 October 2026; CHG-CR325-001): the `ConfigVersion.version` (`configVersion`) of the newest `whitelabel.app_build` (latest `requestedAt`) with `status` `released`, on either platform; its icon is that version's `snapshot` `appIcons.sourceAssetRef` (`whitelabel.config_version`). Null while no build is released.

requiresRebuild.description: True while the draft's source differs from the icon in `liveVersion`, that is when the released version's `snapshot` `appIcons.sourceAssetRef` differs from the draft's `sourceAssetRef`; true when nothing is released (`liveVersion` null) (ADAM CR-325, option A; CHG-CR325-001).

BookingFlowConfig.description: **Set per tenant, with a per-venue override (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-11).** One tenant with several venues (the Kids Club branches, Coastal Aqua beside Union Arena) needs them to differ. The settings in force at a venue are the tenant's, with that venue's entry in `venueOverrides` laid over them field by field. The guest app resolves them for the venue the guest picked (audit R267); `effectiveForVenueId` on `getBookingFlowConfig` returns them resolved.

venueOverrides.description: Per-venue overrides, at most one per venue. A `venueId` that is not one of the tenant's active venues, or appears twice, is refused with 400. An override for a venue later closed is kept and has no effect.

BrandIdentity.description: Every `*AssetRef` here is a `MediaAsset` id from the `assets` library (`createUpload` then `completeUpload`). The image fields are PNG or SVG and at most 2 MB (decided 28 September, audit R270); `introVideoAssetRef` is a video asset within the library's limit for kind `video` (`assets.createUpload`).

logoDarkAssetRef.description: Used on dark backgrounds. Falls back to the primary logo.

logoVariant.description: **Which lockup sits in the nav bar, and whose colours drive the theme (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-4).** `light` uses `logoAssetRef`, `dark` uses `logoDarkAssetRef` (falling back to the primary logo), and `duotone` the two-colour reading of the primary logo.

faviconAssetRef.description: The browser tab icon for the guest web app.

splashImageAssetRefs.description: Splash images, shown in order. Build-time on the native apps (`splashChangeScope`); immediate on web, reaching guests with the publish (audit R163).

splashChangeScope.description: Always `buildTime` for native apps. The guest web app takes a splash change at the publish, with no build (audit R163).

introVideoAssetRef.description: **The optional intro video (decided 29 September, MOB-5).** A video `MediaAsset` from the media library (CMS-010). Streamed, so a change reaches guests with the publish and needs no app build.

introVideoMode.description: When GST-001 plays it full screen. "Skip introduction" is always shown. Anything but `off` needs `introVideoAssetRef`, or 400.

showPoweredBy.description: **"Powered by TICVAI", a configuration toggle, on by default** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q160 and the pre-apply round; consistent with DI-297; CHG-CSA-036). Shown on the launch screen and at the foot of Account and the web footer while true. **Switching it off needs the tenant's licence to allow it**: `setBrandIdentity` refuses `false` with `403 powered-by-locked` unless the tenant's plan carries the `poweredByRemoval` add-on (subscription `LicencePosition.poweredByRemovable`).

primaryArabic.description: Required when `ar` is among the tenant's languages (audit R163). A Latin face alone leaves Arabic in a system fallback that will not match.

secondaryArabic.description: Required whenever `secondaryLatin` is set and `ar` is among the tenant's languages (decided 28 September, audit R163).

changeScope.description: Custom font files are `buildTime`; selecting a bundled face is `runtime`.

FooterConfig.description:
BL-002. **`setHeader` and `HeaderConfig` exist and the footer does not**, which looked like symmetry until you notice it is not: **a header is chrome and a footer is a link surface.**
A footer carries the legal links — terms, privacy, accessibility statement, cookie preferences — and **those are the ones a regulator checks.** Treating it as a mirror of the header would have given it a logo and no way to reach a privacy notice.
**Where it is stored.** `legalLinks` and `copyrightText` are columns of `whitelabel.footer_config`; each entry of `columns` is a `whitelabel.footer_config_column` row and each entry of `socialLinks` a `whitelabel.footer_config_social_link` row. Part of the working draft (see the header). **In the tenant's own database, not the control plane (decided 28 September, audit R163)**: it moved from `control.footer_config` (renamed `whitelabel.footer_config`) and its two child tables.
**Links and order** (R8 blocker WHITE-C24 and IDENTITY-C60): a column's `links` are stored with the column, as one jsonb value in their array order; each column and each social link keeps its `sortOrder`, which `setFooter` writes from its position in the array (0 first), and every read returns `columns` and `socialLinks` ordered by it.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005), written at `tenant` scope by the server.

sortOrder.description: The column's position, written by `setFooter` from the array order (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C60).

links.description: The column's links in display order, stored on the column row as one value (R8 blocker WHITE-C24).

legalLinks.description: **Required links, held separately from the free-form columns** — a tenant reorganising their footer must not be able to remove the privacy notice by accident.

sortOrder.description: The link's position, written by `setFooter` from the array order (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C60).

GuestAppSkinKey.description: The guest app's skins per venue kind, as the approved Mobile App v4 design draws them (`handoff/design-tokens/guest-app.yaml` `skins.byVenueKind`; ADAM CR-280, CHG-R11TEN-007).

GuestPreferences.description:
**What the guest likes, kept apart from what they permit** (consent) and from who they are (the profile). One row per subject. `dietary` and `accessibility` are here rather than as tags because BL-134 gives them their own consent purpose and retention.
**One row per subject, held by a unique key** (ADAM CR-291, option B, decided 29 October 2026; CHG-R11GST-002): a write updates the subject's row, else inserts one.

preferredChannel.description: **Stored on the profile** (`GuestProfile.preferredChannel`) — carried here because the preference screen edits it beside the rest.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

subjectId.description:
Opaque reference. Personal data lives in the separately erasable store, which is what makes erasure possible against an append-only ledger.
**One profile per guest** (ADAM CR-291, option B, decided 29 October 2026; CHG-R11GST-002): unique in the tenant, so `getMyProfile` and `updateMyProfile` read and write the one row of the session's subject. The profile's segment is the one it was first captured in.

preferredChannel.description: Left out where the guest has no preferred channel: a guest who chose `none` in `updateMyProfile` is stored as null and answered without this field (ADAM CR-291, option B; CHG-R11GST-002).

guestLinkId.description: Present where the guest is linked across cells. Marketing acts locally.

engagementScore.description:
22.2.20 and 22.2.21. **`lifetimeValue` and `visitCount` existed, so value was a stored figure and engagement was not.** They are different questions: a guest who spent a lot once and a guest who visits monthly have the same LTV and need opposite treatment.
**Recency, frequency and breadth, not spend** — spend is already `lifetimeValue`, and folding it in here would make one number twice.

engagementTier.description: 5.3.19. **Automatic classification, computed rather than assigned.** `lapsing` is the tier the whole field exists for — **a guest who has not been for a while and still might is the only one marketing can change**, and lumping them with `lapsed` wastes the window.

lifetimeValue.description: **Left out of guest reads until a guest's lifetime value has a currency** (ADAM CR-141, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-007): an amount above a venue is in the currency recorded on its own row (CR-094's rule, which waits on the client), and this row records none yet.

mergedIntoSubjectId.description: **Set on the absorbed profile by `mergeGuestProfiles` and `mergeGuests`**, which retain it as a redirect rather than deleting it. A read that lands here follows it; a second merge of a profile that has one is refused as `alreadyMerged`.

HomepageLayout.description: **The client-approved web and app wireframes are the layout** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q163; CHG-CSA-040): sections, their order and their options follow the approved wireframes and change only where the spec breaks. **Landing-page templates** (workbook Q41 batch 2; CHG-CSA-037): a tenant with no landing page of its own starts from a TICVAI template (`templateKey`, `listLandingPageTemplates`); a tenant with its own site links into the storefront with deep links (`getDeepLinkScheme`, `buildDeepLink`).

templateKey.description: The landing-page template this layout started from (`listLandingPageTemplates`), or null for a layout composed from scratch (CHG-CSA-037).

landingSource.description: `storefront`: this home is the tenant's landing page. `ownSite`: the tenant's own website is the landing page and links in with deep links; this home is still served at the storefront address.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

**Added 20 August.** The table had no key at all — no id, no parent and no natural key, so **no row could be addressed, updated or deleted.** The response schema returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, which is the difference between an API response and a table.

maxItems.description: **How many cards the section shows, the venue's choice** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q152: every customisation option of the approved wireframe, including the card count per section; CHG-CSA-040). Replaces the fixed 1 or 2 highlights of MOB-3: the CMS offers the counts the approved wireframe offers.

scrollAnimation.description: **How the section enters as the guest scrolls** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q153: "must be there"; DI-1088; CHG-CSA-040). Rise, Scale, Slide, Blur or None, as the v4 prototype offers; `none` for guests who asked the device for reduced motion is applied whatever is set.

languages.description: **A tenant may add or select interface languages beyond English and Arabic** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q145; CHG-CSA-039). Any ISO 639-1 language. English and Arabic ship with complete interface strings; for any other, the interface strings come as a TICVAI string pack drafted by AI translation and reviewed (T03), and a string with no translation falls back to English. Content (content pages, banners, promo blocks, FAQ entries and policies) is the tenant's to translate (`translationGaps`); product texts are Catalogue's (ADAM CR-194).

uiStringCoverage.description: How complete the interface strings are in each enabled language (CHG-CSA-039). English and Arabic are always complete; any other language is its `whitelabel.ui_string_pack` row (`UiStringPack`), or `missing` where the language has none (ADAM CR-194).

rtlLanguages.description: The enabled languages written right to left — those whose Unicode CLDR character order is `right-to-left` (Arabic, `ar`, among them). Not configured; it follows from `languages`.

translationGaps.description: Content lacking a version in an enabled language. The content is the tenant's content pages, banners, promo blocks, FAQ entries and policies; an item is missing when a `LocalisedText` of it has no value for the language (ADAM CR-194; see `setLanguages`).

areas.description: The kinds of the missing items, from the closed list `contentPages`, `banners`, `promoBlocks`, `faqs`, `policies` (ADAM CR-194). Stated here rather than as an enum, so a client built on r1, which read a free string, is not broken.

MinimumAppVersion.description:
**The oldest guest app build still allowed to run (decided 28 September, audit R073).** A guest app whose own version is below the one for its platform shows the forced-upgrade screen (GST-047) and nothing else. Null, or a platform left null, forces nothing. Live at once through `setMaintenanceMode`, because an upgrade that must wait for a publish is not forced.

**`storeUrl`** (r8 walk of ticket 27893): the store page GST-047's "Update" button opens, one per platform, set with `setMaintenanceMode` beside the versions and live at once like them. Optional. A store address cannot be derived from `StoreAccount.appIdentifier`, which is a bundle id. The forced-upgrade screen opens the URL for the platform it runs on; where it is null the screen shows the message without the button and the guest updates from the store by hand.

storeUrl.description: The store page of the tenant's app for each platform. https only.

NavigationConfig.description: **The mobile tab set is venue configuration (decided 29 September, MOB-1; 29 September brief decision 6).** Before a tenant saves its own, `bottomNavigation` is Home, Explore, Plan and Tickets (each an `appSection` link), with the Buy tickets button beside them; Map is an optional tab. Plan is left out while `visitPlanner` is off.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

**Added 20 August.** The table had no key at all — no id, no parent and no natural key, so **no row could be addressed, updated or deleted.** The response schema returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, which is the difference between an API response and a table.

isVisible.description: At most five may be visible when `kind` is `bottomNavigation`; the rest overflow. The cap does not apply to `drawer` or `tabs` (ADAM CR-230).

buyButton.description: **The persistent Buy tickets button (decided 29 September, MOB-2).** On every screen of the mobile app except the booking and checkout steps; it opens GST-003. Read with `bottomNavigation`.

style.description: `raised` sits in the centre of the tab bar, as the v4 prototype shows; `hidden` turns it off.

PublishedAnalyticsProvider.x-ticvai-persistence: none — the enabled rows of whitelabel.analytics_provider, guest-facing fields only
PublishedAnalyticsProvider.description: **What the tag loader needs and nothing else** (CHG-GCF-005): no reporting property, no credential, no venue or scope. The values are those of `StorefrontAnalyticsProvider`.

measurementId.description: What the tag or SDK reports to (GA4 `G-...`, Tag Manager `GTM-...`, a pixel id).

consentCategory.description: The cookie category the visitor must grant before this provider loads (marketing-crm `CookieCategory`).

PublishedBanner.x-ticvai-persistence: none — a public projection of whitelabel.banner (r8 walk of ticket 28335)
PublishedBanner.description: One active banner as a guest reads it inside `PublishedTenantConfig`. No state, no schedule dates, no author.

imageUrl.description: The stable address of the banner image.

PublishedPromoBlock.x-ticvai-persistence: none — a public projection of whitelabel.promo_block (r8 walk of ticket 28335)
PublishedPromoBlock.description: One active promo block as a guest reads it inside `PublishedTenantConfig`.

PublishedTenantConfig.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from the current ConfigVersion snapshot and the live status on whitelabel.tenant_config
PublishedTenantConfig.x-ticvai-agreed: 2 October: decided by Chinmay, fix before Block A starts (GFIX-1)
PublishedTenantConfig.description: **The public view of the tenant's configuration** (`getPublishedTenantConfig`, decided 2 October, GFIX-1). The published parts a guest surface renders with, from the current `ConfigVersion`, and the live status `setMaintenanceMode` writes. Nothing a guest cannot see on the page: no draft marker, no CMS counts, no sender addresses, no licensing, no person.

publishedVersion.description: The `ConfigVersion.version` this answer was read from; a client holding the same version keeps its copy.

guestSignIn.description: **What the guest sign-in buttons need before anyone is signed in** (r8, IDENTITY-C21): the public client ids of the tenant's enabled social and UAE PASS providers, derived on read from Identity's provider rows (no stored column, nothing secret). A provider the tenant has not enabled is absent, and its button is not drawn. **Read through `identity#guestSignInProviders`, in process** (ADAM CR-327, part (1), Chinmay, 29 October 2026: "Kind column on sso_provider"; CHG-CR327-001; XDR-021): the tenant's active `identity.sso_provider` rows with `audience` `guest`, each under its `guestProvider` key.

authorizationUrl.description: The guest uaePass row's identity.sso_provider.authorization_url, through identity#guestSignInProviders (CHG-CR327-002).

assetsBaseUrl.description:
**How any guest screen turns an asset id into a picture** (r8 walk of ticket 28156; lead decision of 20 October 2026, option A). The address of a published asset is `assetsBaseUrl` + `/` + the asset id + `/` + a rendition name, for example `{assetsBaseUrl}/{assetId}/card.webp`. The renditions are `thumb`, `card`, `hero` and `original`. Every media object in every guest response carries an asset id and nothing else, so no screen makes a media call per tile. Only public assets referenced by a published version are served at it. `brandUrls` and the banner addresses below are this rule worked out for you.

**Where it comes from** (ADAM CR-327, option A (3), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR327-001): a per-cell setting (`Assets:PublicBaseUrl`), empty until the storage adapter is chosen; the field is left out of the response while it is empty.

brandUrls.description: **The brand assets as addresses a guest can load** (r8 walk of ticket 28335). A guest cannot read `assets`, so the `*AssetRef` ids in `brand` mean nothing to a client. The server turns each asset the published version references into its stable CDN address (`assets.yaml`, `MediaAsset.url`: a public asset has a stable CDN address) and returns it here, beside the ids. Only assets the published version names are resolved; the address is that of the asset version the publish named. A field is null where its ref is null.

skinKey.description: **The asked venue's guest app skin** (ADAM CR-280, option B, 28 October 2026, additive; CHG-R11TEN-007): the published `theme.venueSkins` entry for `venueId`. Null without `venueId`, or where the venue has no entry; the shell then uses the base skin with `park`. **How the shell applies it**: the skin sets every token, then `theme` overrides `--br` (`primaryColour`), `--bg` (`backgroundColour`) and `--ink` (`textColour`) where set; `textColour` is never derived (Theme requires it), and `theme.darkMode` is never used to render. `fonts` replace the skin's faces (`--fh`, `--fb`), with the Arabic pair (`primaryArabic`, `secondaryArabic`) under `dir=rtl`. `--rk` scales the base radii (sm 6, md 10, lg 16, in px) by `theme.cornerRadius / 10`.

banners.description: **The hero and other banners a guest sees now** (r8 walk of ticket 28335): the banners whose state is `active` at the time of the read, by `sortOrder`. Draft, scheduled and expired banners are never returned. `imageUrl` is the resolved address of `imageAssetRef`. Staff read all banners with `listBanners`, which is unchanged. **Read live from `whitelabel.banner`** (ADAM CR-327, option A (2), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR327-001), not from the published version's snapshot: the rows whose state is `active` now, at the tenant root or at the picked venue (`venueId`), so a scheduled banner going live needs no republish.

promoBlocks.description: The promo blocks that are `active` at the time of the read, by `sortOrder`, with the same rule as `banners`. **Read live from `whitelabel.promo_block`** (ADAM CR-327, option A (2); CHG-CR327-001), at the tenant root or at the picked venue (`venueId`).

bookingFlow.description: The booking-flow display settings, resolved for `venueId` when one was sent (the tenant's values with that venue's `venueOverrides` entry laid over, rev 3 CFG-11).

enabledModules.description: The modules the tenant has enabled and published, so a guest surface hides a tab or a homepage section for a module that is off. Licensing is not shown.

enabledFeatures.description: The `featureKey` of every feature toggle that is on in the published version.

analyticsProviders.description: **The analytics platforms the storefront and app load** (Chinmay, 3 October 2026, Pattern 4; CHG-GCF-005): a guest reads them here instead of `listAnalyticsProviders`, which needs `TENANT_CONFIGURE`. The enabled `StorefrontAnalyticsProvider` rows in force for the venue being browsed (that venue's own rows when `venueId` was sent and it has any, else the tenant-wide ones), read live, with only what the tag loader needs. **A provider loads only once marketing-crm `getCookieConsentRuntime` says its `consentCategory` is granted**; before that nothing is sent to it (2.6.58).

paymentTokenisation.description: **The provider the guest app tokenises cards with** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-010; GST-071): the `providerId` `storePaymentToken` requires, its kind and the publishable key the client SDK needs. Never a secret. Null where no provider with tokenisation is connected. **Left out of the response until service sign-in between deployables is built** (#37051, CR-281; ADAM CR-327, option A (4), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR327-001): its read, payments#providerConnectionRecords, takes the service route, and a null would say wrongly that no provider is connected.

TenantAppStatus.description: Computed on read. The published fields come from the current `ConfigVersion`, the maintenance fields from the tenant's `tenant_config` row (`setMaintenanceMode`), and the draft fields from the working draft. **Fields marked staff only are left out of a response to a caller without a staff session** (`getTenantAppStatus`).

isPublished.description: True once any version has been published.

darkAppModules.description: **The app-modules switched off for this tenant** (ADAM CR-164, option A, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-005): their keys (for example `AM-MARKETING-CRM-P01`), from the tenant's release flags. Returned to guests and staff alike; the apps leave those modules' screens out of navigation (the map is `handoff/release-flags.json`). An operation is dark for the tenant only when every app-module that binds it is off, so an operation shared with a live module stays callable. A flag the configuration does not declare counts as on. Additive: nothing new shows on screen.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: Staff only. The working draft differs from the current version's `snapshot`.

activePageCount.description: Staff only. Content pages that are `published` and enabled.

availabilityMessage.description: What the sold-out or closed screen says (WEB-029). Null shows the default wording.

venues.description: **Public: the venues a guest can pick** (decided 28 September, audit R267; schema named 29 September, readiness close-out, our build plan). The source of the venue picker on WEB-001 and GST-001, returned with or without a session. **The active venues, on every read** (ADAM CR-338, venues (a), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR338-001): a venue is listed when its scope node is active (`tenancy.OrgUnit.isActive`), as `TenantConfig.venues` lists them, so `getTenantConfig` and this agree. Ordered by `name`. Empty when nothing is published.

venueId.description: **The venue's scope node** (`tenancy.OrgUnit.id`, level venue): what every guest screen that declares `venueId` `from: session` reads once the guest picks it.

contact.description: The venue's own contact (address, phone, email), from the venue's settings (`tenancy.VenueSettings`, read through `venueSettingsRecords`). Null when the venue has none set; the app then shows the tenant's `contact` (R8 blocker WHITE-C16).

city.description: Shown under the name so two venues with similar names can be told apart. The venue's `VenueSettings.city` (`platform.venue_settings.city`), read through `venueSettingsRecords` (ADAM CR-338, city and openingHoursToday (a); CHG-CR338-001). Null when it is not set.

openingHoursToday.description: Today's opening hours in the venue's time zone, from `tenancy.VenueSettings` opening hours. Null when the venue is closed today or has none set. Today's weekday entry of `VenueSettings.openingHours` (`platform.venue_settings.opening_hours`, jsonb by weekday), read through `venueSettingsRecords`; today is the date in the venue's region time zone (`RegionSettings.timeZone`, `regionSettingsRecords`) (ADAM CR-338, city and openingHoursToday (a); CHG-CR338-001).

whatsNew.description: **Public: the guest "what's new"** (decided 29 September, rev 3 GAP-B2). Newest first, at most 10, from `platform-ops.Release.guestReleaseNotes` of the releases the tenant's cell has received; a release with no guest notes is skipped. Returned with or without a staff session. **Read from the tenant-side copy** (ADAM CR-338, whatsNew (a), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR338-001): `whitelabel.received_release` (`ReceivedRelease`), in the tenant's own database, so a public, cacheable read never crosses to the control plane; newest `receivedAt` first.

publishedAt.description: When the release reached the tenant's cell.

recentChanges.description: Staff only. Names the principal behind each change, so it never reaches a public response. **Derived from `whitelabel.config_version`** (ADAM CR-338, recentChanges (a), 29 October 2026; CHG-CR338-001): one item per version, `area` `publish`, `description` the version's `note`, `principalId` its `published_by_principal_id`, `at` its `published_at`; newest first, at most 10. No new storage.

darkMode.description: **Deprecated and ignored** (Chinmay, 2 October, workbook Q150 and the pre-apply round; CHG-CSA-035). White label has no dark or light mode: the venue's chosen theme is applied, on every device setting. The field is kept so a client built at r1 still parses, is accepted on `setTheme` and returned as stored, and **is never used to render anything or drawn on any screen**; the guest app has no Light/Dark switch.

cornerRadius.description: The prototype's 0 to 22 px slider sits inside these bounds (rev 3 CFG-2, no change). Its named palettes, font pairs and background tones are presets over the colours here and `FontConfig`, not stored values.

surfaceStyle.description: Cards and panels as frosted glass or opaque (decided 29 September, rev 3 CFG-3).

venueSkins.description: **The guest app skin each venue takes** (ADAM CR-280, option B, 28 October 2026; CHG-R11TEN-007): one entry per venue, naming one of the approved app design's skins (`handoff/design-tokens/guest-app.yaml`, `skins.byVenueKind`). A venue with no entry has none set, and the guest app shell then uses the base skin with `park`. `getPublishedTenantConfig` answers the asked venue's entry as `skinKey`.

componentColours.description: **Colours for single interactive elements (decided 17 September, M17-11).** Each is optional and falls back to the theme colours. Every pair passes the same contrast check as the theme (`ContrastProblem`), or `setTheme` refuses it with 400. The guest flow stays the standard one; only the colours change.

VenueContact.description: How a guest reaches the venue: WEB-028 Contact & Venue Information, and the screen shown on an error or when the app cannot help (decided 28 September, audit R073). Public, because nothing here is personal.

openingHours.description: Prose, as the guest reads it. The bookable hours are the catalogue's.
